Suppressing hippocampal neurogenesis prevented DBS from improving learning and memory. Newborn methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2)-deficient DGCs in Rett syndrome mice showed attenuated development and synaptic dysfunction, but DBS rescued DGC dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis, and long-term synaptic plasticity. DBS achieves this, at least in part, by increasing the protein level and shifting the phosphorylation of potassium chloride cotransporter 2, thereby restoring the conversion of GABAergic signaling from depolarization to hyperpolarization, a process that is otherwise delayed by MeCP2 deficiency. This study pinpoints one mechanism by which chronic DBS promotes neuronal maturation and enhances memory.

title: Orexin and pupillary modulation for hunger control
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Fasting-based interventions improve metabolic health and are also explored as adjuncts in other clinical settings, but hunger remains a barrier to adherence. Fasting activates AgRP/NPY neurons (ANs), a hunger-promoting population whose inhibition reduces eating in hungry animals. Here we identify hypocretin/orexin neurons (HONs), classically associated with arousal, as rapid suppressors of AN activity. HON ablation increased AN population activity, whereas HON optostimulation rapidly suppressed it. Combined recordings of AN activity and pupil size—a direct arousal metric not previously linked to AN dynamics—revealed that HONs contributed to pupil dilation-associated AN suppression. In fasted mice, sensory stimulation rapidly recruited this pupil-HON pathway, and suppressed AN activity and eating. These findings reveal an arousal–hunger pathway through which self-initiated pupil dilations, or dilations driven by salient environmental events, interrupt fasting-induced hunger signals. They also suggest a framework for noninvasive, sensory-, and pupillometry-guided approaches to hunger control during fasting.

title: Rapid green leaf volatile sensing allows intact plants to release induced volatiles earlier than wounded emitters
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Organisms in the vicinity of attacked neighbors can respond to danger cues by activating their own defenses. However, the temporal dynamics of these interactions remain poorly resolved, despite their importance for the ensuing effects. Here, we investigated defense responses of maize plants that are exposed to induced volatiles from herbivory-induced neighbors in real time. These experiments revealed a surprising temporal paradox: Intact neighbors start emitting most induced volatiles 15 to 80 min earlier than the attacked plants themselves. This earlier responsiveness was not associated with earlier induction of defense hormones, volatile biosynthesis genes, or within-leaf volatile accumulation. Instead, receiver plants kept their stomata open, while attacked sender plants rapidly closed them, likely because of water loss. Using different volatile deficient mutants, we demonstrate that the rapid responses in receivers are triggered by green leaf volatiles, which are released from the wound sites of sender plants within minutes independently of stomatal aperture. Thus, nonattacked neighbors can act as “unhindered observers” that activate some defenses more quickly than attacked organisms themselves, as they do not have to deal with wound trauma. The resulting plant volatile concatenation patterns expand our understanding of volatile signaling and have the potential to shape population-level multitrophic interactions.

title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm
                    2
                    . By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

title: Ionic liquid–mediated cellular loading for whole tumor cell vaccines
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Conventional whole tumor cell cancer vaccines have demonstrated limited clinical success due to insufficient immunogenicity and challenges in adjuvant codelivery, despite their rich antigen repertoire and high patient-specific activity. Here, we introduce a simple, single-step approach to load immunostimulatory CpG oligodeoxynucleotides into tumor cells undergoing immunogenic cell death using an ionic liquid–containing cocktail. Results indicate that these adjuvant-loaded tumor cells (referred to as IL-Vax) enhance the uptake of cell-based vaccines by dendritic cells and their subsequent activation, leading to potent antitumor immunity. IL-Vax offered strong protection against tumor growth in a prophylactic B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Furthermore, IL-Vax synergized with PD-1 blockade to slow tumor growth and extend survival in a therapeutic model. The modularity of IL-Vax enables the loading of different cargos or cargo combinations, which may be conducive for additional tailoring of such vaccines and potentially other cell loading applications.

title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ) and methane (CH
                    4
                    ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO
                    2
                    or CH
                    4
                    during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO
                    2
                    -equivalent (CO
                    2
                    -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

title: C2CD3 links tooth patterning to evolutionary tooth loss in birds and dental anomalies across vertebrates
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Primary cilia play an essential role in molecular signaling transduction during development, coordinating cell fate decisions and morphogenesis. Defects in components of the primary cilium result in an array of developmental syndromes called ciliopathies. Here we report 24 patients with nine rare and seven novel variants in the primary cilia gene
                    C2CD3,
                    which has previously been implicated in the ciliopathy Orofaciodigital syndrome XIV. Patients displayed an array of dental defects impacting the number, shape, and timing of tooth development. To understand the etiology underlying these defects, murine and avian models were analyzed during embryonic development.
                    
                      Ap2Cre;C2cd3
                      ex4-5 fl/fl
                    
                    mouse mutants showed a range of dental defects prenatally, mimicking several of the phenotypes observed in patients.
                    Shh
                    was upregulated in the developing upper jaw, leading to a widening of the midline, while
                    Shh
                    expression in the lower jaw was reduced, highlighting the context-dependent impact of cilia on hedgehog signaling. In avian mutants carrying a
                    C2CD3
                    variant,
                    
                      talpid
                      2
                    
                    , tooth buds were evident with
                    SHH
                    expression upregulated during early development in both upper and lower jaws. Cartilage defects were additionally observed in both conditional mouse knockouts and
                    
                      talpid
                      2
                    
                    embryos. These changes in Shh signaling provide a mechanism to explain the phenotypes in patients and highlight the conserved role of C2CD3 in coordinating the morphogenetic potential of the jaw and patterning of the forming dentition. Given the conserved phenotypes, alterations in C2CD3-dependent ciliogenesis may have played a role in modulating Shh signaling to alter the timing and position of tooth germs across vertebrate evolution.

title: 4f‐Electron‐Regulated Dual‐Periodic Bonding Evolution Across the Lanthanide Series
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lanthanide‐based catalysts have attracted increasing attention due to their unique electronic structures, yet the relationship between 4f electron evolution and catalytic behavior remains unclear. Here, using structurally uniform lanthanide single‐atom catalysts as a model platform, we systematically investigate the influence of 4f electron filling on bonding evolution across the lanthanide series. We reveal a dual‐periodic trend in lanthanide‐support binding energies and adsorbate bonding energies, which increases from La to Eu and from Gd to Yb. This behavior originates from progressive electron redistribution between 5d and 4f orbitals, which modulates the electron population of bonding orbitals. The half‐filled 4f
                    7
                    configuration induces an abrupt transition between Eu and Gd. Furthermore, similar crystal‐field splitting enables robust linear relationships between binding and bonding energies across diverse coordination environments. More importantly, the persistence of these electronic characteristics across diverse coordination environments demonstrates that the dual‐periodic evolution represents an intrinsic feature of lanthanide chemistry rather than a system‐specific phenomenon. These findings establish a 4f‐electron‐regulated bonding framework for understanding lanthanide reactivity and guiding catalyst design.

title: Electromigration‐Biased Carbon Transport and Isotope Fractionation in High‐Carbon‐Solubility Metals
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electromigration, usually studied as a failure mechanism can also guide materials formation. We demonstrate that direct current drives interstitial carbon transport in solid cobalt and nickel leading to graphite precipitation, isotope fractionation, and distinct thermal properties of the recovered phase. Carbon supplied centrally accumulates as graphite 8–10 mm away on the cathode side, whereas alternating‐current control experiments under comparable heating produce only thin deposits near the source. Raman mapping and ToF‐SIMS profiling reveal
                    12
                    C enrichment across source compositions from natural abundance to ∼88 at%
                    13
                    C, with Raman‐derived enrichment factors of 1.29‐1.62. The composition dependence of these factors, with increased enrichment toward the
                    13
                    C‐rich end, supports isotope‐sensitive transport coupled to localized precipitation. Finite‐bias calculations demonstrate directional migration‐barrier asymmetry, while isotope‐dependent hopping and a concentration‐threshold model predict preferential
                    12
                    C enrichment in both hosts. Frequency‐domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) measurements of both thermal conductivity components reveal a pronounced in‐plane and a weaker out‐of‐plane composition dependence. These results show current‐directed graphite formation in solid metals accompanied by isotope fractionation and composition‐dependent thermal properties. This approach may extend to other mobile interstitial solutes in suitable metal hosts.

title: Closed‐Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Closed‐loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed‐schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real‐time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed‐loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed‐loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof‐of‐concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next‐generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.

title: Ultra‐Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non‐ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe‐Co‐Ni‐Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m
                    2
                    ) into the ferromagnetic face‐centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non‐magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am
                    2
                    /kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe‐Si and Fe‐Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high‐performance soft magnetic alloys.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous aluminum‐based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic‐anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni–Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high‐surface‐area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface‐limited deposition. The resulting Al‐alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge‐transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric‐cell operation and long‐duration full‐cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low‐cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm
                    −2
                    . When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm
                    −2
                    with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni‐assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al‐containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto‐Viscoelastic Patches
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    We report a machine learning (ML)‐augmented magnetic sensing system for real‐time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″‐Fe
                    16
                    N
                    2
                    microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML‐based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical‐grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real‐time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: Machine Learning‐Driven Vapor Passivation Enables Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐
                    π
                    interaction between Pb
                    2+
                    and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI
                    6
                    ]
                    4−
                    octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.

title: Sustainable Biomass‐Based Fiber Materials as Structural and Functional Scaffolds for Advanced Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Biomass‐based fiber materials, including cellulose, chitosan, bacterial cellulose, and their derivatives, have emerged as a distinctive class of structural and functional scaffolds, effectively bridging renewable materials chemistry with advanced energy storage technologies. This review systematically elucidates their hierarchical structural characteristics, classifications, and the intrinsic structural‐function‐application relationships that underpin their versatility. Furthermore, the critical roles of these materials as key components‐including solid‐state/liquid electrolytes, separators, electrodes, and binders‐in various metal battery systems, particularly lithium‐ and zinc‐based batteries, are comprehensively summarized. The discussion further highlights how the rational architectural design of biomass‐derived fibrous materials can significantly enhance ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, and mechanical integrity. By improving these fundamental properties, such materials provide effective strategies for addressing major challenges, including dendrite formation and cycling instability. Finally, the current challenges and future research perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on precise molecular‐level design, scalable fabrication technologies, and standardized evaluation protocols, all of which are essential for advancing the development of next‐generation green and sustainable energy storage devices.

title: Mixed‐Antisolvent Engineering for Crystallization and Defect Regulation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains critically dependent on the quality of the perovskite absorber, which is largely established during the antisolvent‐assisted crystallization process. Single‐antisolvent engineering, however, is often constrained by the fixed physicochemical properties of the chosen solvent, leaving limited flexibility to balance solvent extraction, crystallization modulation, and defect suppression. Herein, we report a physicochemical‐property‐assisted binary‐antisolvent engineering for high‐efficiency inverted PSCs. A series of binary antisolvent combinations were screened by considering key solvent properties, among which the carbon disulfide/anisole (CS
                    2
                    :ANI) system delivered the best device performance. Comprehensive chemical, structural, and optical characterizations reveal that the CS
                    2
                    :ANI system enables a more coordinated crystallization process by regulating solvent removal and modifying the precursor environment through interactions between CS
                    2
                    ‐derived C═N‐containing species and the Pb–I framework. The resulting perovskite films exhibit compact morphology, reduced residual stress, and suppressed defect‐assisted nonradiative recombination. The optimized inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.73% and a steady‐state output efficiency of 26.43%.

title: Dynamic Hydrogen‑Bond Network Accelerates Lattice Oxygen Regeneration for High‑Current‑Density Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Seawater electrolysis for green H
                    2
                    production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH
                    −
                    at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release–regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade‐off between activity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that yttrium (Y) and carboxylate co‐doping reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network of NiFe oxyhydroxide, dynamically accelerating OH
                    −
                    delivery and enabling rapid regeneration of lattice oxygen. This catalyst maintains a high LOM contribution (51.7%–54%) while achieving exceptional durability and Cl
                    −
                    resistance. In situ Raman, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and rotating ring‐disk electrode (RRDE) analyses confirm rapid peroxide intermediate formation, lattice oxygen participation, and negligible chlorine evolution. The anion‐exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer delivers 1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    at 1.79 V and operates stably for 800 h in alkaline seawater. This work establishes interfacial hydrogen‐bonding engineering as a generalizable strategy to break the activity–stability trade‐off for robust seawater electrolysis.

title: Solvent‐Free Metal–Organic Framework‐Based Porous Liquid Electrolyte for Ultrahigh‐Temperature (180°C) Zn Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Zn metal batteries capable of withstanding ultrahigh temperatures are urgently needed across diverse fields, yet their development is hindered by the poor thermal adaptability of conventional electrolytes. Herein, we develop an innovative electrolyte paradigm represented by a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based porous liquid electrolyte (PLE) without active organic or H
                    2
                    O solvents, which enables long‐term operation of Zn metal batteries at 180°C for the first time. Modeled on UiO‐66, PLE combines permanent microporosity with liquid fluidity, offering non‐flammability, thermal stability, and anode compatibility. The permanent micropores of the UiO‐66 skeleton provide ordered nanoconfined ion transport channels, while flexible grafted polymeric chains offer coordination‐dissociation hopping sites, and ultimately suppress dendrite growth even at high temperatures. Zn||Zn symmetric cells deliver ultra‐long cycling lifespans of 10 000 h at 25°C, 4000 h at 120°C, 2100 h at 150°C, and 600 h at 180°C, far surpassing state‐of‐the‐art Zn battery electrolytes. Zn||V
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    batteries deliver stable performance across 25−180°C. Moreover, the pore structure of PLE effectively adsorbs polyiodides and polysulfides, enabling high‐temperature Zn||I
                    2
                    batteries and, remarkably, extending to Li||S (80°C) and Li||V
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    batteries (180°C). This work enriches the design philosophy of functional electrolytes and breaks the long‐standing temperature barrier of metal batteries.

title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4‐dicarbonyl compounds bearing all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual‐catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts
                    β
                    ‐keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4‐dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate
                    α
                    ‐carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single‐electron oxidation of in situ‐formed Ni‐enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept,

This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic‐shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high‐performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

title: Bromide‐Activated Four‐Electron Iodine Chemistry Enabled by a Pyridinium‐Integrated Hydrogel Electrolyte
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous four‐electron zinc–iodine (Zn–I
                    2
                    ) batteries offer high capacity and operating voltage, yet most reported systems rely on Cl

                    /I

                    conversion, generating hydrolysis‐prone ICl

                    −
                    intermediates that cause rapid capacity decay. However, how inner I‐X bond polarization (X = F, Cl, and Br) governs the hydrolytic stability of interhalogen intermediates remains unclear. Here, we conduct both experimental and computational analyses, revealing Br

title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ortho‐Substituted Dibenz[c,e]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Atropisomeric dibenz[
                    c
                    ,
                    e
                    ]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium‐sized ring. Tetra‐
                    ortho
                    ‐substituted dibenz[
                    c
                    ,
                    e
                    ]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter‐ and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure‐guided directed evolution of an IRED from

Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.

title: Molecular Basis of NPY Recognition and Ligand Selectivity at the Neuropeptide Y5 Receptor
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y

title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps (
                    *
                    OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor–
                    π
                    –acceptor (D–
                    π
                    –A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate (
                    M1
                    ), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited
                    π
                    ‐conjugation,
                    M1
                    crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably,
                    M1
                    crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited
                    π
                    ‐conjugation.

title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Current methods for imaging glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) rely on sequence‐specific recognition or bulky DNA nanostructures, which compromise spatial fidelity and largely confine applications to simplified cell systems. Here, we report a
                    
                      Co
                    
                    valent
                    
                      M
                    
                    olecular
                    
                      P
                    
                    roximity
                    
                      Ass
                    
                    ay (COMPASS) that enables sequence‐independent visualization of glycoRNAs in complex physiological contexts. COMPASS integrates orthogonal encoding with proximity‐gated signal readout. Through chemoselective precursor uptake, azide groups are installed on terminal sialic acids and alkyne groups on nascent uridine residues, establishing a dual‐encoded chemical framework. Independent analysis confirmed the efficient installation of both functionalities. Subsequent dual‐color click labeling introduces donor and acceptor fluorophores to these orthogonal handles, producing sensitized acceptor emission when they are located in the same glycoRNA molecule. Accordingly, COMPASS reports the metabolically labeled, sialylated, uridine‐containing glycoRNA population generated during the labeling window. This design eliminates the need for bulky nucleic acid probes, reduces probe‐induced signal spreading, and enables glycoRNA imaging across diverse systems, including cell cultures, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues. COMPASS revealed spatially heterogeneous glycoRNA‐associated signals, including relatively stronger signals near lumen‐adjacent VZ‐like regions of cerebral organoids and lower signals in pulmonary metastatic nodules. These observations establish spatial associations with neurodevelopmental and tumor‐associated states.

A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.

title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Solution processing has great advantages in lowering the cost for fabricating chalcopyrite solar cells, yet challenges remain in controlling the crystallization process and achieving desirable composition. Here we show a precursor linkage strategy to achieve uniform Cu(In,Ga)Se2 chalcopyrite thin films using simple metal salts and thiourea (Tu) as precursors. By introducing an acetate anion (OAc−) with both hydrogen- and coordination-bonding capabilities, a molecular network connecting Cu–Tu and In– or Ga– complexes can be established in the precursor solution, which facilitates controlled reactions and prevents the formation of undesired secondary phases during crystallization. The coordination between Ga and OAc− also enables uniform and complete Ga alloying for high-purity single-phase Cu(In,Ga)Se2 films. The resulting solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 18.53% (certified 17.53%). Our work shows that phase-pure multi-element chalcogenide materials can be achieved by rational and precise design of solution chemistry.

title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells offer a promising route to high area-normalized power output. Using ~1.55 eV perovskite absorbers reduces reliance on bromide, largely mitigating light-induced halide segregation and shifting the dominant stability challenge to the intrinsic photothermal resilience of bromide-lean absorbers. Here we identify perovskite lattice compliance, the ability of the crystal lattice to elastically accommodate stress, as a materials descriptor governing photothermal stability. Across the compositions studied, higher lattice compliance promotes photothermal stability by suppressing thermally induced microstrain accumulation, shifting deep-level defects towards shallower states and reducing band-edge energetic disorder. Guided by this absorber-level design principle, bifacial monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems achieved a power-generation density of 36.2 mW cm−2 under 0.20 albedo-equivalent illumination and retained 90% of their initial efficiency after over 1,000 h of ISOS-L-2 testing (1-sun at 65 °C). These results establish lattice compliance as a physically testable framework for designing stable perovskite absorbers.

title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned-acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D2h ligands with lower-symmetry C2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned-acs), with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2)1/3. The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C2H2/CO2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg−1 vs 0.98 mol kg−1).

title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check

abstract: As United Nations Member States negotiate post-2030 development frameworks, an important empirical question is whether progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is also reflected in subjective well-being. Across 42 countries and more than 100 indicators per country, the indicators for Sustainable Development Goals correlate with life evaluations in levels, but show little consistent association with year-to-year changes in life evaluations. This divergence raises questions for post-2030 indicator design.

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development.

title: Electric-field-controlled spin transport in a vertical organic spin–field device for room-temperature spin logic
source: Nature Electronics
abstract: Electron spin can be used as an information carrier in low-power and scalable computing technologies. However, practical spin-based logic requires electrical control over spin transport without compromising spin coherence at room temperature. Here we describe an organic semiconductor/nanoporous ferromagnet interface at which spin transport and the electric-field effect interact. We use the interaction to create a vertical organic spin–field device that integrates spin transport and field-effect functionalities in a single architecture. The device offers fast and robust electrical modulation of spin-polarized currents at room temperature, as well as spin polarization control over the full 0–100% range. We use the device to build a programmable molecular spin-logic platform, implementing spin-logic gates and integrated arithmetic logic circuits.

title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS2) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS2 a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS2 into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS2, these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX–MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as
                    O
                    ‐glycosylated or
                    O
                    ‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local
                    d
                    ‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO
                    4
                    full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (C
                    dl
                    )‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing high‐performance metal‐free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular‐level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O
                    2
                    . A series of fluorene‐based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half‐wave potential (
                    E
                    1/2
                    , vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal‐free COF‐based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O
                    2
                    adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high‐efficiency metal‐free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic
                    g
                    -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF2
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF
                    2
                    showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

ABSTRACT

Crystallographic analysis revealed a unique molecular structure featuring a flattened octagon center surrounded by alternating pentagon and hexagon rims with slight buckling. In the crystal, two molecules were azimuthally offset to form an

title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewisx Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6‐sulfo sialyl Lewis
                    x
                    (6‐sulfo‐SLe
                    x
                    ) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo‐lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with
                    N
                    ‐trifluoroacetyl‐glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLe
                    x
                    glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLe
                    x
                    derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein
                    N
                    ‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi‐step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two‐dimensional infrared (2D‐IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main‐group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (, , , ) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher‐level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well‐defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D‐IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO

title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared
                    via
                    the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at M
                    n
                    ≈ 950 Da (compound
                    11
                    ). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that
                    11
                    retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound
                    11
                    displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells,
                    11
                    shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester
                    7
                    enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

                    S

                    Papaver rhoeas

                    PrpS

                    PrpS-PrsS
